## Legal Moves

Treat a valid argument like a *legal move* in a game. Today we collect the
moves: eight named rules, and the traps that look like rules but are not.

You will use them on Monday, to spot rules, build proofs, and design traps of
your own.


## Warm Up

A *valid argument* is a *legal inference*. Content can change; form is what makes it valid.

- If the lab is open, I’ll go. The lab is open. **So I’ll go.** 

- If the exam is today, the forum is quiet. The forum isn’t quiet. **So the exam isn’t today.** 

---

## Rule Card: Modus Ponens (MP)

<div class="card rule">
From <code>p→q</code> and <code>p</code>, infer <code>________</code>.
</div>

**Ex:**  
If the bus is full, I’ll walk. The bus is full. **________**


::: notes
Blank: q      Example: So I'll walk.
:::

---

## Rule Card: Modus Tollens (MT)

<div class="card rule">
From <code>p→q</code> and <code>¬q</code>, infer <code>________</code>.
</div>

**Ex:**  
If office hours moved, Slack has an announcement. No announcement. **________**


::: notes
Blank: ~p      Example: So they didn't move.
:::

---

## Rule Card: Hypothetical Syllogism (HS)

<div class="card rule">
From <code>p→q</code> and <code>q→r</code>, infer <code>________</code>.
</div>

**Ex:**  
If tidy then joins are simpler; if simpler joins then faster viz; **________**


::: notes
Blank: p->r      Example: So tidy => faster viz.
:::

---

## Rule Card: Disjunctive Syllogism (DS)

<div class="card rule">
From <code>p∨q</code> and <code>¬p</code>, infer <code>________</code>.
</div>

**Ex:**  
Dinner is sushi or tacos. Not sushi. **________**


::: notes
Blank: q      Example: So tacos.
:::

---

## Rule Card: Conjunction / Simplification

<div class="two-col">
<div class="card rule">
<strong>∧-Intro</strong>: from <code>p, q</code> infer <code>________</code>
</div>
<div class="card rule">
<strong>∧-Elim</strong>: from <code>p∧q</code> infer <code>________</code>
</div>
</div>


::: notes
Blanks: ^-Intro p^q      ^-Elim p (or q)
:::

---

## Rule Card: ∨-Intro

<div class="card rule">
From <code>p</code> infer <code>________</code>.
</div>

**Ex:** I rode my scooter today, **________**

**Note** validity cares about *form*, not plausibility of the added disjunct.


::: notes
Blank: pvq      Example: So I either rode my scooter or I'm a unicorn.
:::

---

## Rule Card: Resolution (RES)

<div class="card rule">
From <code>p∨q</code> and <code>¬p∨r</code> infer <code>________</code>.
</div>

**Ex:**  
Either study or soccer; if study then library. **________**


::: notes
Blank: qvr      Example: So soccer or library.
:::

---

## Rule Card: Constructive Dilemma (CD)

<div class="card rule">
From <code>(p→r), (q→s), (p∨q)</code> infer <code>________</code>.
</div>

**Ex:**  
If sunny then picnic; if rainy then museum; sunny or rainy; **________**


::: notes
Blank: rvs      Example: So picnic or museum.
:::

---

## Fallacy Cards (flash)

<div class="two-col">
<div class="card rule">
<strong>Affirming the consequent</strong> ❌  
<code>from p→q, q infer p</code>
</div>
<div class="card rule">
<strong>Denying the antecedent</strong> ❌  
<code>from p→q, ¬p infer ¬q</code>
</div>
</div>

---

## Validity

**∧-Elim**: $(p\wedge q)\rightarrow p$ is this always true?


## INValidity

**Affirming Consequent**: $((p\rightarrow q)\wedge q)\rightarrow p$ is this always true?


| $p$ | $q$ | $p\rightarrow q$ | $(p\rightarrow q)\wedge q$ | $((p\rightarrow q)\wedge q)\rightarrow p$ |
|---|---|:--------:|:--------:|:--------:|
| F | F |       |      |      |      
| F | T |       |       |       |       
| T | F |       |       |       |       
| T | T |       |       |       |


---

## Micro Rule Cards {.smaller}

Keep these next to you. You will need them Monday.

:::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
- **MP**: from `p→q, p` infer `q`
- **MT**: from `p→q, ¬q` infer `¬p`
- **HS**: from `p→q, q→r` infer `p→r`
- **DS**: from `p∨q, ¬p` infer `q`
- **∧-Intro**: from `p, q` infer `p∧q`
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
- **∧-Elim**: from `p∧q` infer `p` (or `q`)
- **∨-Intro**: from `p` infer `p∨q` (any `q`)
- **RES**: from `p∨q, ¬p∨r` infer `q∨r`
- **CD**: from `(p→r), (q→s), (p∨q)` infer `r∨s`
:::
::::

**Common traps:**

:::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Affirming consequent: `p→q, q ∴ p` ❌
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
- Denying antecedent: `p→q, ¬p ∴ ¬q` ❌
:::
::::
